purpose: Authoritative-vendor evidence delta promoting Limble CMMS and UpKeep from discovery-queued to spec-verified only. Reuses existing REST, SCIM and webhook components, records version/authentication/data/value boundaries, and does not enable writes or claim sandbox/tenant evidence.

patch.evidenceNote: Current Limble documentation confirms its v2 HTTPS API, clientID/client-secret credentials carried as Basic authorization, page/limit pagination, API-access-backed extraction, SCIM v2 provisioning endpoints with distinct US, Canada and 21 CFR base URLs, and configurable webhook endpoints for assets, asset fields, tasks and purchasing objects. WFM uses only read API operations and inbound event receipt; SCIM provisioning and webhook/API configuration remain management/write surfaces. Region/compliance endpoint selection must be explicit and credentials remain executor-bound. No Limble tenant or credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Limble API credential limited to the approved reporting/read use case where the customer's plan and role model permit it
explicit region/compliance endpoint binding for SCIM: US, Canada or 21 CFR as applicable; never auto-switch between them
SCIM use is read/reconciliation only for WFM until provisioning is separately authorised and certified
webhook configuration is performed out-of-band by an authorised Limble administrator; the WFM runtime only receives approved events
dataAvailableOrExpected: locations and site hierarchy exposed by the v2 API
maintenance tasks including work orders, planned maintenance and work requests where exposed to the API credential
parts and purchasing context where enabled
users/groups through documented SCIM integration and account data surfaces
task, asset and purchasing change events where the customer's webhook configuration exposes them
automationOpportunities: convert open/planned maintenance demand into technician headcount and skill requirements before shifts are finalised
correlate completed-task duration and asset history with labour standards, overtime and maintenance productivity
use location and asset IDs to reconcile CMMS demand to WFM sites/work centres without duplicate master-data setup
combine API pagination checkpoints with event-driven change signals so maintenance staffing stays current without excessive polling
reconcile users/groups through SCIM while keeping employment and qualification truth in HCM/WFM
savingsHypotheses: reduce emergency overtime and contractor callouts by exposing planned and emerging maintenance workload to workforce planning earlier
reduce paid idle time by coordinating maintenance windows with production staffing and executable line availability
reduce implementation effort by reusing Limble location/asset identifiers and existing API/SCIM structures
improve maintenance labour standards using observed task completion duration and asset history instead of static assumptions
dataGaps: public Limble material does not establish a dedicated API read-only scope model for every endpoint; effective credential permissions must be tenant-proven
API/integration availability depends on the customer's Limble plan
employment contracts, payroll, absence and authoritative qualifications normally remain outside Limble
customer asset/task custom fields require schema discovery and mapping
webhook delivery guarantees/signature behavior are not sufficiently documented in the reviewed public material and require authorised evidence
constraintsRisks: API keys are managed by Super Users, so the credential must not be assumed least privilege merely because WFM issues GET requests
SCIM is inherently provisioning-capable and its regional endpoints differ; provisioning remains disabled and endpoint pinning is mandatory
API pagination uses page/limit and must be checkpointed/deduplicated for large asset/task datasets
webhook configuration is administrative and stays outside runtime authority
customer-specific task/asset fields and multiple locations require canonical identity reconciliation
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI, SCIM and signed-event profiles. In an authorised Limble environment, bind the correct tenant/region, prove the minimum API credential against representative GET locations/assets/tasks, test pagination and custom-field schema fingerprints, validate read-only SCIM reconciliation and webhook authenticity/delivery behavior, then normalise maintenance/site/asset demand before promotion beyond spec verification.

patch.evidenceNote: UpKeep's current v2 API reference confirms an Enterprise-plan REST API, session-token authentication derived from an UpKeep user, pagination/filtering, work orders, assets, locations, requests, preventive-maintenance triggers, users, parts/custom fields and webhook configuration. The same API is strongly write-capable, including work-order/request/user/asset mutations and webhook creation. WFM therefore requires a dedicated least-privilege user whose effective read behavior is tenant-proven, blocks all mutations in the connector, treats webhook subscription configuration as management-plane authority, and respects documented endpoint deprecations/version differences. No UpKeep account was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated UpKeep integration user with the minimum effective visibility required for approved work-order, asset, location, request and maintenance reporting reads
session token stored only at the executor boundary and rotated/expired according to the vendor session model
no POST/PATCH/DELETE authority in the WFM read connector even though the same API/session can expose those operations
webhook creation/update is performed separately by an authorised administrator; runtime only receives approved event types
dataAvailableOrExpected: work orders including status, dates, assignees/teams, asset/location, response time, time/cost, parts and custom fields
assets, locations and vehicles where used
maintenance requests including status, requester/team/asset/location and linked work-order relationship
webhook events for work orders, PM work, requests and purchasing where configured
automationOpportunities: translate open and preventive maintenance work into future technician/skill demand and likely overtime exposure
use response time, completion time, cost and assignment context to improve maintenance labour standards and workforce forecasting
coordinate maintenance workload with production schedules and machine-state evidence to reduce planned/unplanned disruption
use requests and work-order status events as early signals for staffing redeployment or maintenance escalation
reconcile asset/location/team IDs to WFM/ERP/MES entities while preserving UpKeep custom-field mappings
savingsHypotheses: reduce emergency overtime by forecasting technician demand from open requests, work orders and preventive-maintenance triggers
reduce downtime by matching maintenance workload to available qualified labour and production windows
improve labour-cost attribution using work-order time/cost/assignment data alongside WFM payroll and shift records
reduce manual maintenance-to-workforce reporting through direct read integration and event-driven reconciliation
dataGaps: public documentation describes session tokens generated from a user but does not establish a separate immutable read-only API token class
employment contract, absence, payroll and broad qualification truth remain outside UpKeep
worker/user identifiers, teams and custom fields require customer-specific mapping to HCM/WFM identities
a complete current rate-limit contract is not established in the reviewed public reference and must be tenant/sandbox proven
constraintsRisks: the same v2 API exposes many mutative endpoints, so intended GET-only behavior is not permission proof; effective user permissions must be tested
API changelog includes sunset/deprecated maintenance endpoints and spelling/version transitions, so endpoint capability/version discovery is mandatory
webhook registration is mutative and remains outside the normal read connector
pagination, include-expansions and custom fields can make payloads large and require bounded queries/checkpoints
session authentication originates from user credentials and therefore requires dedicated service identity, secure rotation and no personal-user dependency
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI and signed-event profiles. In an authorised UpKeep Enterprise environment, create or identify a dedicated least-privilege integration user, prove GET-only effective behavior and session expiry, enumerate current v2 endpoint/version capability, test pagination/filtering/custom-field handling and representative work-order/asset/request reads, validate webhook authenticity/replay/dedupe after out-of-band subscription setup, and normalise maintenance demand/cost/assignment data before promotion beyond spec verification.
